title: Jury in Lindsay Clancy trial now allowed to consider manslaughter charge
dek: Closing arguments are underway in the trial of Lindsay Clancy in Massachusetts. A judge has allowed the jury to consider a manslaughter charge. The case centers on the deaths of three children and raises questions about postpartum psychosis as a legal and medical factor.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: A Massachusetts judge has cleared the way for jurors to consider a manslaughter charge in the trial of Lindsay Clancy as closing arguments proceed, spotlighting postpartum psychosis, a rare psychiatric emergency affecting 1 to 2 per 1,000 women after delivery.
bottom_line: The trial is proceeding to jury deliberation with the manslaughter option now available. No timeline for a verdict or details of the prosecution's counter-arguments to the postpartum psychosis defense are provided in available reporting.
body: Closing arguments are underway in the trial of Lindsay Clancy in Massachusetts, with a judge signaling on Wednesday that jurors will be permitted to consider a manslaughter charge following a defense request, according to NBC News reporting.

The case centers on the deaths of three children and raises questions about postpartum psychosis, a severe psychiatric condition. According to CBS News, postpartum psychosis affects only 1 to 2 per 1,000 women after delivery. The condition is described as a mental health emergency affecting a person's sense of reality, characterized by delusions, hallucinations and confusion, per the same reporting.

Perinatal psychiatrist Dr. Uruj Kamal Haider, cited by CBS News, described postpartum psychosis as "a break from reality" where "the brain cannot properly process information." The delusions in the condition, according to Dr. Haider's account in CBS News reporting, are "fixed false beliefs that tend to revolve around the baby." CBS News reports that postpartum psychosis is a psychiatric emergency where the mother must be sent to the hospital and the baby put into a safe place as soon as possible. With adequate and prompt treatment, according to Dr. Haider in CBS News reporting, most women with postpartum psychosis recover and have "wonderful, beautiful lives with their family."
